investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness or lifecycle checks required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity (no free VM slots), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 125 s (remote-agent-create), 143 s (remote-agent-state), and 144 s (remote-agent-runtime) before each eval timed out. Because the pod never started, the runner never wrote any evidence, causing a total contract gap across all 4 required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool in the production-api cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods.
[Likely] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm label from a previously sufficient count to only 2, exhausting capacity faster than before.

[Possible] The pod's node affinity/selector is overly restrictive, targeting only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes while excluding 4 others that could potentially be configured to support the resource but are not currently labeled or tainted appropriately.

[Possible] A quota or resource limit on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource at the namespace or cluster level is set too low relative to concurrent probe demand (all 3 sibling checks ran near-simultaneously and each requires its own VM slot).
[Less likely] A node or VM provider configuration change caused the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable count to drop to 0 on one or both eligible nodes, making the effective pool smaller than expected.

Introduce a concurrent scheduling stress eval that submits multiple remote-agent pods simultaneously to detect capacity contention between sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) that run near-simultaneously in the same probe window.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was left unscheduled for 125–144 seconds. The scheduler reported 0/6 nodes available: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, with no preemption victims available. Because no agent pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner could not create a remote agent, and therefore produced zero evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state. The eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905) never returns a live agent, so the probe times out and emits no evidence, causing the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to be entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-create: same scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck for 125s — confirms the capacity problem predates the remote-agent-state check.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: contract at line 264 requires ['orgId', 'agentId', 'readyState', 'state'] — none were present in the run output.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: the cluster's peer-pod VM slots are fully consumed, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning only 2 of 6 nodes are even eligible, and those 2 are at capacity. A recent node label change or pod spec drift could have reduced the eligible node pool.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads are competing for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the two eligible nodes, transient exhaustion could occur without a persistent misconfiguration.

Lower confidence — node affinity selector on the remote-agent pod spec is overly restrictive: if the selector was recently tightened (e.g., by a deployment change), fewer nodes would qualify, amplifying the impact of any VM slot consumption.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes cluster shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the two affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different cause (e.g., API-level agent creation failure) would need to be investigated.

If the pod spec's nodeAffinity/selector is found to have been recently changed to exclude nodes that previously matched, the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a misconfiguration in the pod scheduling constraints.

If the scheduler message is absent from a re-run and the failure message changes (e.g., to an API timeout or authentication error), the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion would not be the active cause.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on the Kubernetes cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, so VM slot exhaustion is surfaced as its own signal rather than inferred from a pod scheduling timeout.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness or lifecycle checks required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity (no free VM slots), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 125 s (remote-agent-create), 143 s (remote-agent-state), and 144 s (remote-agent-runtime) before each eval timed out. Because the pod never started, the runner never wrote any evidence, causing a total contract gap across all 4 required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool in the production-api cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods.
[Likely] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm label from a previously sufficient count to only 2, exhausting capacity faster than before.

[Possible] The pod's node affinity/selector is overly restrictive, targeting only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes while excluding 4 others that could potentially be configured to support the resource but are not currently labeled or tainted appropriately.

[Possible] A quota or resource limit on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource at the namespace or cluster level is set too low relative to concurrent probe demand (all 3 sibling checks ran near-simultaneously and each requires its own VM slot).
[Less likely] A node or VM provider configuration change caused the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable count to drop to 0 on one or both eligible nodes, making the effective pool smaller than expected.

If the pod's node affinity/selector were found to be misconfigured to exclude all 6 nodes (not just 4), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a misconfigured affinity rule, and the '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message would be a secondary symptom.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was left unscheduled for 125–144 seconds. The scheduler reported 0/6 nodes available: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, with no preemption victims available. Because no agent pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner could not create a remote agent, and therefore produced zero evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state. The eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905) never returns a live agent, so the probe times out and emits no evidence, causing the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to be entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 143s.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150323, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-06T12:39:37.810Z — the check ran well past the 143s unschedulable window before failing.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, readyState, or state was ever written, confirming the agent pod never reached a running state.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent returned.

sibling.remote-agent-create: same scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck for 125s — confirms the capacity problem predates the remote-agent-state check.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler error, pod stuck for 144s — confirms the capacity problem persisted through the entire eval run window.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1905 immediately after acquiring orgId — if the pod never schedules, no agent identity is returned and no evidence can be written.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: contract at line 264 requires ['orgId', 'agentId', 'readyState', 'state'] — none were present in the run output.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: the cluster's peer-pod VM slots are fully consumed, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning only 2 of 6 nodes are even eligible, and those 2 are at capacity. A recent node label change or pod spec drift could have reduced the eligible node pool.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads are competing for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the two eligible nodes, transient exhaustion could occur without a persistent misconfiguration.

Lower confidence — node affinity selector on the remote-agent pod spec is overly restrictive: if the selector was recently tightened (e.g., by a deployment change), fewer nodes would qualify, amplifying the impact of any VM slot consumption.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-06 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: 0/6 nodes are available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. Because no pod could be scheduled, the remote agent VM was never created, and the eval never reached the point of collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector for remote agent pods. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all, and the 2 that do match have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod request is immediately marked Unschedulable, the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval probe times out without producing any evidence output. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and it is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-level failure.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not exhausted, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If the Unschedulable error disappears on a re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a prior eval pod released its slot between runs) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the 4 nodes that currently do not match the pod's affinity/selector are shown to have been recently relabeled or tainted, the primary cause would be node affinity drift rather than kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion.
If a re-run of the eval with AURA_STATUS_CHECKS=remote-agent-runtime passes and returns all 5 required evidence fields, the scheduling issue has self-resolved and no capacity intervention is needed.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass on a subsequent run, the failure is not a shared scheduling bottleneck and a check-specific issue should be investigated.
